from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Review 2D vectors and area.", "2x2 determinant defines area.", "This builds the cross product."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: Vectors and Determinants", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5 + UP * 0.5, color="#FF5733")
        v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.5 + UP * 1.5, color="#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        matrix = Matrix([[r"a", r"c"], [r"b", r"d"]], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B5')
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        det_val_pos = Text("ad - bc", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(det_val_pos, 'E5')
        self.play(Write(det_val_pos))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 2D Pseudo-Cross Product", [
            "2D cross product isn't standard.", 
            "Signed area tracks orientation.", 
            "Positive: counter-clockwise turn."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3388FF"))
        v = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color="#3388FF")
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C3')
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#3388FF").next_to(v.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8833"))
        # Define pseudo-cross product v_perp (rotate 90 counter clockwise)
        v_perp = Vector([-0.5, 1.5], color="#FF8833")
        self.place_at_grid(v_perp, 'C3')
        v_perp_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}^\perp", color="#FF8833").next_to(v_perp.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(v_perp), Write(v_perp_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#88FF33"))
        # Indicate rotation from v to v_perp
        arc = ArcBetweenPoints(v.get_end(), v_perp.get_end(), angle=PI/2, color="#88FF33")
        self.play(Create(arc))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the 3D Cross Product", [
            "3D cross product is perpendicular.",
            "Use 3x3 determinant.",
            "Result is a new vector.",
            "It defines rotation axis.",
            "Follows the hinge orientation."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        vec_a = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#33FF57")
        vec_b = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#33FF57")
        vec_c = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        
        vectors = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b, vec_c)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_a), FadeIn(vec_b), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        det_text = MathTex(r"\det \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ a_x & a_y & a_z \\ b_x & b_y & b_z \end{pmatrix}", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(det_text), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_c), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Rotate(vectors, angle=PI/4, axis=UP), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#33FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF88FF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Anti-commutative property: a x b.", "Calculates physical torque force.", "Computes 3D surface normals."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # 1. Summarize 3D cross product formula
        formula = MathTex(r"\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = -(\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{a})", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Display area calculation application
        torque_label = Text("Torque: " + r"\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(torque_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(torque_label), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Highlight cross product usage in vector fields
        normal_label = Text("Surface Normal: n = a x b", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(normal_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D Intuition to 3D Geometry

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors and Determinants
sections.content: Brief review of 2D vectors and the 2x2 determinant (ad-bc), which serves as the building block for the cross product calculation. Visualizing the area of a parallelogram.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2x2 grid representing a 2D parallelogram spanned by vectors (a,b) and (c,d).

sections.title: The 2D Pseudo-Cross Product
sections.content: Explain that the cross product is strictly a 3D operation, but in 2D, we compute the 'z-component' (scalar) representing the signed area. Positive for counter-clockwise, negative for clockwise.
sections.example: A squirrel running on a plane: the sign of the cross product tells us if the squirrel is making a left turn (+) or a right turn (-).

sections.title: Defining the 3D Cross Product
sections.content: Introduce the cross product result: a vector perpendicular to the original two. Define the formula using the 3x3 determinant with unit vectors i, j, k.
sections.example: An animation of two flat rectangular plates meeting at a hinge; the cross product vector emerges from the hinge pointing along the axis of rotation.

sections.title: Geometric Meaning: Right-Hand Rule and Magnitude
sections.content: Explain that the magnitude |a x b| = |a||b|sin(θ), representing the area of the 3D parallelogram. Use the Right-Hand Rule to determine the direction.
sections.example: A robotic arm joint: curling your right fingers from vector A to vector B, your thumb points in the direction of the cross product, indicating the axis of the joint's movement.

sections.title: Summary and Application
sections.content: Quick recap of properties (anti-commutative: a x b = -b x a) and real-world application in physics (Torque) and 3D graphics (Surface Normals).
sections.example: A character in a video game holding a wrench; calculating the torque on a bolt using the cross product of the lever arm and the force vector.
